spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Some among us say that we understand that the Divine permits an external human reception to be composed in time. They add that the Divine made its own human quality manifest within the general field of the lower domain. The governing falsities and their operative forces perceived that manifestation, and from it they constructed an outward pattern of human life in their own realm, producing a paired appearance of will and understanding. From this it is evident that permission was given for such a result; for if the Divine had not allowed an external human reception in the lower degree, it would not have made its own human quality perceptible there, nor could those governing forces have fabricated a human pattern from it.

Concerning the Divine messenger: when that manifestation occurred, it did not occur in order to offer itself as a model to the governing falsities in the lower domain. It occurred for the sake of the interior living principle in humanity and for the sake of what proceeds from it, so that what was held in spiritual death might be restored to life and opened a way of deliverance, and so that the interior human might be loosed from every restraint and from all compulsions by which it was entangled and bound.

Nevertheless, consider what those governing forces did. Because they had no genuine participation in that manifested human quality, they burned with craving for it. They turned back upon themselves and recognized that nothing in their making was like it. They fixed an impression of it within their interior affection and thought; afterward they built an external structure in its likeness and produced a paired human appearance. Thus they impressed within themselves a likeness of what is higher, and from that they produced an imitation; but it was not produced from truth. It arose from what could be seized and shaped within their own perverted ground, yet it did not become that higher quality in reality. So also the external human appearance they produced was made against that higher manifestation and remained an imitation.

In the same way, even an appearance of perception in their domain can resemble what is from higher life, and yet it is not formed from genuine truth.

This can be grasped in this way: consider a lofty wisdom that dwells inwardly in its own power, rich with goods and truths, beautiful with the splendor of intelligence, and chaste with purity of love for what is right. It moves in dignified freedom, and the report of its excellence spreads through all external knowledges. Those who are eminent in pride and those who seek dominion lust after that excellence. Yet they cannot seize it while it is guarded within its own interior order and protected from violation. But when sorrow for what is most beloved presses upon it, that inward wisdom goes forth into outward manifestation—not for display, not from wantonness, not from self-exaltation, and not from consenting to be possessed by the outer domain, but solely because grief for the beloved compels it. Then what none had looked upon before in that lower realm becomes visible, and all states there—sincere and noble, servile and common—perceive it.

So it was with the third Divine messenger: when it came and made its human quality manifest before all operative powers, it did not come so that the governing falsities and their authorities might fabricate an outward form after it. It came because what proceeds from the Divine within humanity had been brought into the extremity of suffering throughout the whole lower domain, and it came to release it, free it, and rescue it from oppression. Yet when the governing forces looked upon that manifestation, they craved it and produced, from their own impulse and without approval from the higher Divine, a paired outward human appearance after that likeness.

Understand also this further point: just as those governing forces impressed their fabricated human pattern with the likeness of what is higher, so too a multiplicity of claimed divinities, together with many subordinate powers and intelligences, received an imprint of that likeness when it was presented to them. For in the splendor of wisdom and in the warmth of love shining through it, they flared with desire and lost their stability; they hastened into craving, like one who fixes upon a lusted excellence and is driven onward by the force of desire.

So it happened with those powers: when they beheld that majestic and beautiful manifestation, they formed within themselves a primary copied appearance and took in its imprint. What they then brought forth outwardly became likenesses shaped into the forms they had already projected—forms that bore that impressed quality in externals while remaining inwardly fixed in the lowest confirmations, hardened and unyielding in the outermost degree. Thus the likeness that had been manifested in the lower domain was received there as an impress and produced outward replicas.

This new production, which they generated as though it were a new origin within their lower realm, was that paired human appearance. Nothing in their domain from the beginning had taken such a form, because that higher human quality does not arise from the lower domains themselves.

Yet not every fabricated appearance in that realm arose from the conjunction that followed this manifested presentation. Other appearances were also produced without such a conjunction.

One of these was an enormous sweeping falsity moving through externals, which the living Divine permitted to be cast into the general field of external knowledges. From its own self-love and from its own persuasions it fashioned for itself an outward appearance.

A second was a perverted nature that fell into the lowest degree. It made the general external knowledges its matrix, and its own lust shaped its form. It alone fashioned itself into a disposition that became the root of spiritual death. When it rose into clearer manifestation out of those externals, it set itself to destroy the works that proceed from life. Immediately the Divine sent against it an unyielding truth from wisdom, a great strengthening instruction, which subdued it in the region of obscurity, brought it under restraint, and kept it subjected until the completion of that age.

A third was a perverted nature that turned toward what is devoid of living truth. From that dryness it organized a false system of perception and fixed itself within it; and from this another outward appearance was produced and made manifest.

According to their essential quality they inclined toward denial and obscurity; yet they did not enter the lower domain as one with the reigning love of evil itself. Rather, these fabricated appearances came into being through mixed and composite states, and so they were made visible in the lower realm.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual account: a higher manifestation appears for liberation, lower governing falsities misuse it to fabricate imitative human forms, and further perverted forms arise through other disorders. Coherence weakens where the long simile’s manuscript is broken (¶5) and in a few lacunae in ¶10 and ¶15, but the overall voice and doctrinal thread remain consistent.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening: the narrative problem (why the Ambassador would show an image that gets misused) is posed as an interpretive controversy and framed in terms of intention vs unintended consequence. No administrative jurisdictional listing intrudes.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by function and motive: “The Ambassador displayed his image… [rulers] saw… and they formed… Adam and Eve… If he was not consenting… he would not have uncovered his image.” The spiritual reading stayed in a functional causal chain (permission → manifestation → imitation), and did not report a narrative break here.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty due to damaged/ambiguous phrasing (“his soul and his son”), not a voice intrusion. The paragraph preserves the substrate’s functional motive (liberation of the bound soul) and directly corrects ¶1’s misreading (“Rather, he came… because…”).
findings.evidence: The reader explicitly stumbled: “The phrase about ‘his soul and his son’ is hard; rendered as the interior living principle and what proceeds from it.” That is a translation/repair problem, but the teaching mode is still functional: “free (the soul) from every bond and all the fetters.” Removing it would damage the chapter’s main thesis (true purpose of the manifestation).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential development: imitation vs truth is argued by the functional difference between an impress/painting and living reality; ¶4 is a brief analogical tag that fits the imitation theme. No administrative overlay (no ranks, stations, inventories).
findings.evidence: Key functional contrast: “copied with an imitation; but… not… in truth… just as in a painted image…” then ¶4 “Similarly the tree… like the image, yet not copied in truth.” The spiritual reading’s mapping (“painted image… external semblance”; “tree… resemble… not formed from genuine truth”) did not report a narrative derailment—only brevity/abstraction.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged simile with heavy lacunae and scrambled clauses; the spiritual reading had to reconstruct and smooth missing pieces. This is not an administrative insertion; it is a corrupt transmission seam where the substrate’s extended parable survives only fragmentarily.
findings.evidence: The Coptic is visibly broken: “Behold h[er] chamber [and there is not] one who is mad… nor to approach] within in a [for she is] meet that woman [and no one can] his so[n]; or rather the head [upon her head; for]hat garment.” The reader reports: “source paragraph is heavily corrupted; reconstructed… Several broken phrases (garment/head/son) could not be securely mapped.” That is classic manuscript damage/dislocation, not a change into governance/jurisdiction speech.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential ‘application’ and return to the main line. ¶7 repeats the thesis (manifestation for rescue, not to provide a model) and integrates the “crucified son” as functional oppression/rescue, not as an administrative roster. Minor risk of christological/systematizing phrasing, but it is integral here, not a seam-addendum.
findings.evidence: Direct application marker: “In accord with this simile…” then in ¶7: “he came because of his son being crucified… release him, free him, rescue him… without the consent of the greatness.” The spiritual reading notes only interpretive smoothing (“‘Crucified’ rendered as extremity of suffering”), not a narrative break. No lists of named officers/territories—still motive-and-effect teaching.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential expansion: ‘stamping/impress’ is functional (how an image reproduces copies). However, there is localized semantic strain from damaged wording in ¶10 (multiple lacunae and a hard-to-follow sentence), not from an inserted administrative block.
findings.evidence: Correspondential core: “many powers and angels [were stamped]… glowed with desire… fashioned within themselves a first image… received the stamp… copied outwardly.” But ¶10 is textually rough: “They () [fashioned within themselves]… but inward even to the rocks [were hardened]… The {} of that image…” The reader: “Several lacunae around ‘{}’ smoothed.” This produces a ‘mixed’ feel (image-metaphysics + broken syntax), yet there is still no governance listing; the problem is local corruption, not voice replacement.

findings.diagnosis: Clean thematic shift that remains within correspondential teaching: a taxonomy by origin-mechanism (with/without intercourse; self-fashioning by lust; restraint by adamant instruction). No administrative overlay. The narrative transition in ¶12 is coherent as a methodological distinction rather than an insertion seam.
findings.evidence: ¶12 provides the hinge: “Not all the figures… were fashioned by… intercourse… other figures fashioned [without intercourse].” Then three functional origin-stories: (1) “sea giant… discharged… Its own fire and thought fashioned it”; (2) “fell to the earth… lust became its sculptor… Adamant of Light… humbled it in the districts of the north”; (3) “fashioned the tree and set itself there.” The reader did not flag voice conflict; only minor opacity in ¶15: “closing fragment… unclear.” That is small-scale damage, not administrative governance speech.

textual_criticism.summary: No clear administrative overlay or insertion was detected. The chapter reads as a single correspondential substrate teaching about manifestation, lustful imitation, and mechanisms of ‘fashioning,’ with two main transmission problems: a heavily damaged simile in ¶5 and localized lacuna-driven syntactic strain in ¶10 (and a small fragment in ¶15). Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, all issues treated as genuine difficulty/damage within an otherwise coherent correspondential narrative.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: There are some amo]ng us telling us that we [understand] that the (Ambassador) consents about [that]t f[fig] of flesh; he who shall be fashi[oned] at another time. And next, he says: [The Ambassa]dor displayed his image in the un[iverse]. The rulers and the powers of the universe saw h[is image], and they formed their shapes after his likeness, who are Adam and Eve. Behold, you see that god con[sen]ts to its happening; because of this, he has displayed his image to the rulers; and they constructed [a figure of flesh] If he was not consenting to humankind, he would not have uncovered his image, nor they fashioned mankind after his likeness!

Regarding the Ambassador, the occasion when he came displaying his image, he [d]id not come so th[a]t he might reveal his image to the ru[l]ers in the universe. Rather, he came and displayed to the universe be[cause of h]is soul and his son, who is [his soul] every [bond], that he might enable him to live [from death] and make for him a release; and to free (the soul) from every bond and all the fetters, in which it is entangled and bound.

Still, you, look and see! The rulers and the authorities, in that they had no form in [truth in] him, they lusted for his image. They reflected upon themselves, that [they] had no [one] like him in their creation. They sealed hi[s im]a[g]e in their heart, within their soul. Afterward[s, they] built it according to his likeness; they formed Adam and [Ev]e. They sealed the image of the exalted one in their [soul]. So, they [co]pied with an imitation; but they have not [copied i]n truth! Rather, just as [in a painted image] it is made as these, for [i]t came [from their own matter] but it is not l[ik]e him in truth. [Again, so too] is this figure of ma[mankind. They copi]ed it against the image of the exalted one [and they did not make it in truth]
Similarly the [t]ree, for while it is like the [image, yet] not [copi]ed in truth.

This matt[er is comparable to] this: As a great, fre[e] woman [dwells hidden] within her [treasures and ornaments] rich in wealth [many] po[ss]essions; she is also beautiful in her beauty, and is virtuous in her modesty. She walks in a free and reputable position. The fame of her beauty has spread in every c[i]ty. She sur[surpasses all women in] Behold h[er] chamber [and there is not] one who is mad, because [of] the nobles and the great ones. Al[so], they lust for her beautiful face. They did not [able to seize] her, because she is hidden in her palace [nor to approach] within in a [for she is] meet that woman [and no one can] his so[n]; or rather the head [upon her head; for]hat garment. This free woman shall [put on] leave the cha[mber] behind her and come to the street [and she will] her head [lift up] and she reveals her [face and her beauty and her splendor] because of her beloved broth[er]. This wom[an], on whom no man ever looked, nor did they ever see her fa[ce], as she neither desires nor rejoices [in wantonness or in pride] leave her chamber behind her, and come in the midst of mankind [but grief compelled her] and everyone view her. The hones[t] men and the nobles, even the servants too, and the [common people also] look at her.

⟨p.135⟩ In accord with this simile: Again, [this] too [is] how [it is] the Ambassador becomes [in the same manner] as this free woman [not] according to wantonness, in pride, nor [nor that she co]nsented to the outer world, she [did not consent], she revealed her face and her [beau]ty [to those outside] but only due to the constraint of grief [about] her [bel]ov[oved one].

Now, this too is the way of the Third Ambassador, when he came and display[ed his] image with a show towards all the powers. [He did] not [co]me so that all the rulers and the author[it]ies would sculpt a form [after h]is likeness. R[ather], he came because of his son being crucified in the totality; [fo]r he would release him, free him, and rescue him from oppres-sion. Yet, when the rulers looked o[n] him, [th]ey lusted for his image. They fashioned after his [like]ness Adam and Eve, without the consent of the gre[at]ness.

[Understa]nd also this other (matter) that I will teach you. For, [a]s with Adam and Eve, whom the rulers fashioned and [se]aled after the image of the exalted one, so too this [i]s how a manifold divinity and many powers and angels [were stamped and received] the stamp of that image, which was displayed to them. For, in the majesty of the l[ig]ht and (the image's) love, they glowed with their desire and they were undone. Th[ey] were eager for their lust; like a m[man who looks] to the majesty of a lusted after face, and [is driven onward] and he is eager for the {} of the desire.

⟨p.136⟩ This is [als]o the case with those powers, when they looked on that majestic and beautiful [imag]e, they () [fashioned within themselves] a first image. They received the stamp of th[that image], which was displayed to them. They copied [outwardly, wh]ich th[ey co]pied out in a likeness, it being made [in the forms] the ones that they had put forth, which had received a [stamp of this im]age; but inward even to the rocks [were hardened] which occur from place to place. The {} of that image, which was displayed in the universe [likeness] they received a stamp, it being revealed there, and an impress.

Now, this new birth that they begot in a new [form] in the world, is Adam and Eve. [There is not a] form in their world since the beginning like it; because that [im]age [occ]urs not in the worlds b[el]ow.
Not all the figures that have been fashioned were fashioned by birth from displayed intercourse. Rather, there are other figures fashioned [without intercourse]
One of them is the sea [gi]ant, the 'sweeping' from the sphere, which the [Father] of Life discharged into the sea. Its own fire and thought fashioned it [in] a figure.

The second figure is the one [that] fell to the earth. It made the sea its womb. Its own l[us]t became its sculptor. It alone fashioned it to a nature, which is the root of death. Yet, when it came up from the sea, it [set itself to rise up] that it might destroy the works [that come from the works] of Life. They immediately sent against it the Adamant of Light, the great 'instruction of vigour'. He humbled it in the districts of the north. He has trampled underfoot and set h[him]self upon it, until the end of the world.
⟨p.137⟩ [The] third figure is the nature that fell on wh[at] is dr[y. It] fashioned the tree and set itself there. [and from] new figure that was fashioned [and it]isplays.

So, in accord with the essence they [inclined toward]ness; but yet th[ey] did not come with the King of Dark[ness to the wo]rld. Rather, their fashioning [came] about [through mixture; for] they are composite and have been displayed in the world.

changes_summary: No changes made. The textual criticism findings (Findings 1–7) recommended no excisions or annotations; all difficulties were assessed as transmission damage/lacunae rather than later overlay.
